series.name: SHOP TALK
series.tagline: The business of tech, from the barbershop.

cast.name: Scoop
cast.bio: Brings the story and the receipts. Thirty years inside enterprise tech, zero patience for hype.

cast.name: Unc
cast.bio: Has run The Shop for 34 years. Every story ends with one question: who's getting paid?

cast.name: Keys
cast.bio: Builds the systems everybody else is talking about. Translates the tech so nobody gets fooled.

cast.name: Dre
cast.line: Okay, but how do I get paid?
cast.bio: Creator, reseller, future mogul. Turns every headline into a side hustle, for better or worse.

cast.name: Miss Pearl
cast.bio: Taught economics for 36 years. Owns more dividend stocks than anybody in the room. Says less, lands more.

episodes.title: The $115 Billion Question
episodes.dek: Nvidia just posted its biggest quarter ever, five days after its founder-CEO resigned.

tiles.alt: Dre, in a barber chair, turns to Scoop as he walks into the shop with a tablet while Unc holds clippers. Dre: Scoop! Nvidia's CEO stepped down. They finished, right? Scoop: Not even close, young man. Title: The $115 Billion Question.
Scoop shows a rising bar chart to a stunned Unc and Dre. Scoop: Five days later, they reported $115.8 billion. In one quarter. Unc: Billion? With a B?!
Keys explains from the waiting bench with her laptop. Keys: $107.6 billion of it is data centers. Every AI company is buying their chips. Scoop: Gold rush. Nvidia sells the shovels.
A thoughtful Scoop with Unc behind him under an orange neon scissors sign. Unc: So the money's right. But who's driving the bus? Scoop: The CFO, for now. The board is still searching for a new CEO.
Unc spreads his arms over his busy shop. Unc: I tell my barbers: if this shop can't run without me, I don't own a business... Scoop: ...you own a job. Wall Street calls it key-person risk.
Dre holds up his phone as Scoop laughs and Miss Pearl peers over her glasses. Dre: Say less. I'm buying Nvidia tonight! Miss Pearl: Baby, you still owe Unc for last week's cut.
SHOP TALK end card with Scoop's portrait and the cast. Sources and the full breakdown at hicksnewmedia.com/shoptalk.

facts: Revenue: $115.8B for the quarter ended Oct 25, up 103% from a year ago.
Data center: $107.6B, up 110%. That's about 93% of Nvidia's sales.
Leadership: Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; the board says it will not reinstate Huang.
Outlook: Q4 guided to $130B (±3%), with no China data center compute revenue assumed. FY28 growth outlook raised to about 75%.
episodes.why: Record results during a leadership vacuum tell you the product and the customers are strong. They don't tell you who sets the next five-year bet. That's key-person risk, and it applies to a trillion-dollar chipmaker and a four-chair barbershop the same way.

episodes.title: Meet the Family
episodes.dek: Every Tuesday, the business of tech gets argued out at The Shop. Here's who's in the chairs.

tiles.alt: Family portrait of the SHOP TALK cast inside The Shop barbershop: Unc seated in a barber chair, Scoop and Keys standing behind him, Dre crouched in front, Miss Pearl seated with a newspaper. Unc: Welcome to The Shop. Title: Meet the Family.
Scoop, a bald man in black glasses and a camel tweed blazer, holds a tablet by the shop window. Scoop: No hype. Just the facts. Scoop, the Newsman.
Unc, the gray-bearded owner in a burgundy vest, leans on his barber chair with arms folded. Unc: Follow the money. Unc, the Owner.
Keys, an engineer with locs and gold hoops, works on a sticker-covered laptop on the waiting bench. Keys: Show me the specs. Keys, the Engineer.
Dre, a young man in a cream hoodie, films himself with his phone and a ring light. Dre: Okay, but how do I get paid? Dre, the Hustler.
Miss Pearl, in cat-eye glasses and a lavender cardigan, peers over her newspaper. Miss Pearl: Baby, sit down. Miss Pearl, the Teacher.
SHOP TALK end card with Scoop's portrait and the cast. Episode 01 drops later today at hicksnewmedia.com/shoptalk.

episodes.why: SHOP TALK takes one business-of-tech story a week and argues it out at The Shop: six panels, one lesson that outlasts the headline.
